cases.name: unknown-child-of-sequence
cases.description: An invented tag inside <sequence>. It used to validate and run: check said "is valid", exit 0, and the tag did nothing. <env> has always answered this.

cases.name: unknown-child-of-switch
cases.description: Self-closing on purpose: the walk skipped anything that was not an open/close element, so this exact spelling passed while <bogus></bogus> was caught.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="p" local="en"><sequence name="K"><gen type="text" value="a,b"/></sequence><switch name="S" on="K"><bogus_tag/><case is="a"><data>1</data></case><default><data>2</data></default></switch></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: unknown-child-of-distinct
cases.description: A <distinct> wrapper inside a sequence groups <gen>s; its own body was never looked at.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="p" local="en"><sequence name="A"><distinct><gen name="p" type="number" value="1..9"/><gen name="q" type="number" value="1..9"/><bogus_tag/></distinct></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: unknown-child-of-pool
cases.description: Same skip as <switch>: neither branch of the pool member loop said anything about a name it did not know.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="p" local="en"><pool name="P" count="3"><bogus_tag/><sequence name="f"><gen type="text" value="x,y,z"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="A"><gen type="number" value="1..9"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: unknown-child-of-fixture
cases.description: A fixture holds text and <line>s. Anything else was ignored unless it was a generator inside a <line>.

cases.name: unknown-child-of-block
cases.description: A <block> holds <line>s. Rust accepted an invented tag here in silence — a hole left when the other containers were closed, and one the full report hid: it only showed when the brief output put the implementations on one line each.

cases.name: a-fixture-body-that-would-render-nothing
cases.description: A <data> written straight into a fixture, with no <line> around it. The validator used to skip it and the renderer only ever walks <line> children, so the text was dropped without a word — the config said something and got nothing. Named rather than rendered: a bare <data> would have to invent whether it ends the line, and <line><data> already says.

cases.name: a-second-env-is-refused-not-dropped
cases.description: Both `<env>` and `<block>` are read by taking the FIRST of their kind, so a second one is dropped whole — every sequence it declares, every line it lays out — and the run finishes looking healthy while half the config produced nothing. `check` called such a document valid. The same silent discard TDC014 refuses for the self-closing spelling, one level up. Reported on the SECOND one, which is the surprise.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="a"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="x"/></sequence></env><env count="2" seed="b"><sequence name="B"><gen type="text" value="y"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{A}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-second-block-is-refused-not-dropped
cases.description: Both `<env>` and `<block>` are read by taking the FIRST of their kind, so a second one is dropped whole — every sequence it declares, every line it lays out — and the run finishes looking healthy while half the config produced nothing. `check` called such a document valid. The same silent discard TDC014 refuses for the self-closing spelling, one level up. Reported on the SECOND one, which is the surprise.

cases.name: an-invented-tag-inside-an-env-level-uniq-group
cases.description: The children of an env-level <uniq>/<distinct> were checked by the reference alone. The four ports declared the list and never read it, so an invented tag inside a group was accepted in silence — the very hole the unknown-child work was meant to close.

cases.name: member-was-never-a-tag
cases.description: `<member name="…"/>` sat in the allowed-children lists of all five and was read by nothing: it slipped past the unknown-child check, the group then wrapped no sequences, and the author got TDC221 — a warning about the symptom. Never designed, never documented, in no fixture. Removed, so it is refused like any other invented tag.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="s" local="en"><sequence name="A"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence><sequence name="B"><gen type="text" value="1,2"/></sequence><uniq><member name="A"/><member name="B"/></uniq></env><block><line><data>${{A}}${{B}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-data-loose-in-a-pool
cases.description: A pool publishes NAMED fields, so a bare <data> has nothing to address it and rendered nothing at all. The composed form works one level in, inside the member's own <sequence>.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><pool name="P" count="2"><data>lead-</data><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="R"><gen type="pool" value="P"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R.a}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-data-loose-in-env
cases.description: The same in <env>: nothing renders it, and the walk used to skip a <data> child before any check ran.

cases.name: a-data-loose-in-a-block
cases.description: A <block> holds <line>s. A <data> beside them rendered nothing while the page promised it was an error.

cases.name: a-data-loose-in-tdc
cases.description: The outermost of the four. Same rule: a <data> joins the value around it, and at document level there is none.

cases.name: a-known-construct-at-document-level
cases.description: A <sequence> written straight into <tdc>. Found while closing the loose-<data> hole: the document-level walk called every stray tag UNKNOWN in four of the five, so a construct the language knows was reported as one that does not exist. TDC013 says where it belongs; TDC010 is for a typo.
cases.config: <tdc><sequence name="loose"><gen type="text" value="a,b"/></sequence><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="a"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{a}}</data></line></block></tdc>
